title: Made 124 female RPG portraits so far - what classes or archetypes am I still missing?
author: VortexAssetStudio
selftext: Hey everyone.I've been grinding away at a big pack of realistic female portraits (medium bust, mostly frontal/semi-frontal) meant for RPG dialogue boxes, party rosters, and strategy games. Right now I'm at 124 portraits. I tried to split them between "good/righteous" and "corrupted" versions, covering mostly dark fantasy (vampires, blood witches, valkyries, nobles), some sci-fi/cyberpunk (androids, cyborgs, infiltrators), a few post-apoc scavengers, and elemental/ascended forms for late-game bosses or class upgrades.Before I start generating the next batch to wrap this up, I'd love to hear from devs who actually buy or use portrait packs: what specific roles, factions, or vibes do you usually struggle to find for your UI?

comments.author: Shrineheart
comments.body:
A mix of different races and body sizes would be nice. Right now you have a lot of variety in vibes and themes but not the actual woman herself.
Disclaimer here, I don't buy portraits but I know a lot of folks who do DND and fantasy games and I've done a lot of research for my own game on general character design stuff.
Variety and customizability will get more eyes on things generally speaking and it's something a lot of players would like to have.

Like, this set seems a lot like a series of generic kind of dolls because of the lack of variety. Severe looking woman with either white, black or brightly colored hair in a spandex suit or armor with themed costume elements.

I'm not trying to knock you down here, btw, like I legitimately have worked on doing DND portrait packs and stuff I want to make a customizable tool for it in the future.

People like options. You can keep that same pose and set up while varying the person more. The vibes they give off. Is she charming? Is she warm? Is she snide? Is she thin or fat or muscular? Does she have freckles or moles or beauty marks? Scars? Eye patch? Unique hair styles? Glasses or eyewear? Jewelry? Piercings? What kinds of clothes might she wear? They don't all run around in catsuits. There's a huge world of fashion to take inspiration from!

This, at first glance, looks like the same stern white lady over and over.

replies.author: VortexAssetStudio
replies.body: this is honestly super helpful feedback . thank you. Looking at the grid as a whole, you're totally right. the facial structures and expressions ended up way too uniform while I was focused on varying the outfits and themes. Adding distinct expressions, ages, scars, and more grounded clothing styles is definitely going to be the main priority for the next batch.

replies.author: Shrineheart
replies.body:
Yeah, it's easy to fall prey to it even in traditional art. In my game I literally set up a randomizer with a bunch of skin, hair, and eye colors and picked age groups based on population in an area.

Oh! Hair texture differences and black hairstyles are also good additions. Age variations like you mentioned. Buff old grandma blacksmith looking lady is going to make me more interested just because novelty/variety.

And color palettes. As an artist there's like a TON of color palette references and stuff out there. You can get some really interesting designs with just colors you wouldn't have thought to use! I'm not sure what kind of model you're using etc but if you can give reference colors that would be a cool one to mess with too.

replies.author: VortexAssetStudio
replies.body: "Buff old grandma blacksmith" is honestly an instant winner.NPCs with that kind of lived-in character and specific craft vibe are almost impossible to find in standard asset packs. The randomizer approach for age groups and diverse hair textures makes total sense too, especially for worldbuilding. really appreciate you taking the time to share all this, it gives me a much clearer direction for what to build next

replies.author: Shrineheart
replies.body: No problem! Look forward to seeing the results!
